items.title: 66086_Zilner T. Randolph oral history interview
items.q: she said the German told her

ctx.x: Yes. See, my mother was a seamstress. She was a professional seamstress and something happened to her machine and she had to send for this technician to come and fix it. And at the time he came she told me -- she was still pregnant with me -- so she said the German told her, he says, 'Now, that, if the baby be a boy, name him Zilner, and spell it z-i-l-n-e-r.' And so she wrote that down and so she named me Zilner.
